_notes: M2.3's labelled retrieval evaluation set, expanded from M1.2's 20-query
relevance set. Queries carrying "m1_2": true are that original set verbatim,
so the published headline number stays computable and comparable while the
wider suite diagnoses *where* retrieval fails rather than only whether it does.
Categories, per SCOPE §5.1: exact_id, paraphrase, temporal, correction,
"expect" is the object that should rank in the top k. "expect_absent" is an
object that must NOT appear at all — a stale fact a correction superseded, or
another project's object. A hit rate obtained by also returning the superseded
answer is not a retrieval win.
Written and labelled before being measured against any implementation.

corpus.content: I prefer fixed-point integers in minor units over floating point doubles for representing money.
Ledger rounds monetary amounts exactly once, at presentation time, never during arithmetic.
Always display currency amounts with the ISO 4217 code, not the symbol.
Always show me the failing test output before proposing a fix.
Ledger's test suite runs under pytest with asyncio_mode set to auto.
Ledger should not merge a pull request that drops line coverage below 85 percent.
I run Python 3.12 and manage every project with uv rather than pip or poetry.
I want mypy configured strict on every project, with type annotations on all public functions.
Use ruff for both linting and formatting; do not add black or isort separately.
Ledger stores its data in Postgres with pgvector, not in a dedicated graph database.
Write plain SQL migration files; do not introduce an ORM migration tool into Ledger.
Ledger deploys to Fly.io from the main branch on every merge.
Ship the invoicing module before the end of the quarter.
The first invoicing release supports one-off invoices only; recurring billing is explicitly out of scope.
Chris is independent and consults through his own studio rather than working for an employer.
Chris is based in Washington DC and works in the US Eastern timezone.
Chris works late in the evening rather than early in the morning.
Do not schedule anything before 10am; mornings are for focused work.
Write in plain declarative prose. No bullet-point summaries unless I ask for a list.
Comments should explain why a decision was made, not restate what the line does.
The Atlas prototype is written in Rust.
Atlas is paused until Ledger's invoicing work lands.
For web interfaces I use plain server-rendered HTML with a little vanilla JavaScript, not React.
Design REST endpoints around nouns and HTTP verbs; avoid RPC-style action URLs.
Never put credentials in a repository; read every secret from the environment.
In code review, tell me the single most serious problem first instead of listing everything at once.
Do not add a new dependency unless the reason survives being said out loud.
Raise a specific exception with a useful message instead of returning None on failure.
Every storage and retrieval call in my projects is async, all the way down.
Chris drinks his coffee black and does not take sugar.
Ledger's Postgres runs on host port 5433, not the default 5432.
ledger/money.py holds the Money value type and its arithmetic.
Ledger embeds with nomic-embed-text at 768 dimensions.
The CI workflow file is .github/workflows/verify.yml.
All of my open source work ships under the MIT licence.
Chris works at Acme Corp.
Chris is independent and consults through his own studio.
Ledger stored its data in MySQL during the prototype.
Ledger moved from MySQL to Postgres in March.
Ledger deployed to Heroku when it launched.
Ledger now deploys to Fly.io on every merge to main.
I never use an ORM in Ledger; every query is written as plain SQL.
I don't use Docker for local development, only in CI.
I don't want database tests written against mocks.
Never introduce module-level mutable global state.
Beacon is written in Go.
Beacon stores events in SQLite rather than Postgres.
Beacon deploys to a Raspberry Pi on my home network.
Atlas has never been deployed anywhere; it is a prototype.
Priya owns the invoicing module.
Priya works from Lisbon, in Western European Time.
I own the money and currency code myself.
Nothing ships in Ledger without the module owner's review.
Chris drinks his coffee black, no sugar.
I prefer tea in the afternoon and coffee in the morning.
I donate a fixed share of my income to charity each year.
I like Rust but would not choose it for a web backend.
For web backends I reach for Python with FastAPI.
